rv.q: The second does not feel as potent or dangerous, the comedy and clipped period accents neutering the threat.
Faithfully done, effectively performed, but it feels like a prelude to something yet to come, in this case, Richard Jones’ revival of The Birthday Party later this summer .
This Pinter double bill once more proves the venue to be a powerhouse of regional drama.

cn.t: Pinter's psychological one-acts earn praise for their dark humor and astute performances, though the slippery exploration of truth, lies, and betrayal in bourgeois relationships proves more intriguing than fully satisfying.
